regex_tests.citation: section 600.2912b of the Michigan Compiled Laws
Michigan Rules of Professional Conduct, Rule 1.7
Barkley v City of Southfield, ___ Mich App ___; ___ NW3d ___ (2026) (Docket No. 369608)
regex_tests.matched_label: Unpublished Court of Appeals opinion (Michigan style, by docket number)
Michigan Administrative Code (also Bare Michigan rule number, context_required)

regex_notes: The MRPC regex misses 'Prof.' (it accepts only 'Professional', 'Prof'l' or 'Profl'); allow 'Prof(?:essional|'?l)?\.?'. It also misses ', Rule N.N' after 'Conduct'; allow ',?\s*(?:Rule\s+)?'. The blank-slip form '___ Mich App ___' is not matched by the Mich Reports regex. Only the docket clause catches it, under the 'Unpublished' label, even for a published opinion. The route still reaches Justia, so the miss is harmless, but the label is wrong. Allow '(?P<volume>\d{1,3}|_+)\s+Mich…(?P<page>\d{1,4}|_+)' as the lv den pattern already does.
overall: 15 rows: 8 confirmed, 1 failed, 6 still-blocked (the MCR, MRE and MRPC rows, bound volumes, opinions and MSC orders, all on courts.michigan.gov and now blocked for every route under the Disallow: / policy). The worst consequences: (1) Michigan court rules, evidence and conduct rules have no permitted text source. Justia, LII and public.law do not carry them. (2) Official Mich App pagination and MSC leave orders are now absent. (3) The citation map still routes case law, rules and subsequent history to blocked rows first. (4) mi-mcl-html's objectName pattern serves an unrelated object (E.R.O. 2007-2). (5) The mi-mcl-pdf built URLs are gated and the shell is refused, so a new citation was untestable. (6) The Justia MCL pattern breaks for acts without divisions.
